steps.intro: Judge here: does the deck now look and behave like part of YouCoded, and is it calm enough? Each row quotes your comment and shows before and after. Press a tile to open its picture large.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Your round-7 comment, and what changed

calls.call: Attachments is now a copy of the app's Deliverables card: one tile per picture, with a preview on top and its name below.
calls.why: Pressing a tile opens the full-window picture popup. Before, the pictures were laid out large inside the card.
calls.decided: "i wanted these too look like 'deliverables' which meant a single card for each image. clicking that should open our popup image screen/comment menu"

from: Chat → Deliverables card: header line, sideways strip, tile size, open-arrow
new: A comment count on a tile's corner
reuse.note: Sizes are the app's own: tiles 224 wide, previews 112 tall.

calls.call: The picture popup shows one picture with its comments beside it. You drag across the picture there to comment on a part of it.
calls.why: You no longer drag on pictures inside the card. A clip plays in the same popup.

calls.call: The "New this round", "Changed from your comment" and "Settled" badges are gone. Rows sit under plain headings instead: New, Changed, Already settled.
calls.why: The only coloured pills left are real statuses such as Passed and Unclear, and a card's answered state.
calls.decided: "these ' new this round' and 'changed from your comment' badges don't really make much sense, not to mention the colors make them visually confusing next to the unclear/pass/fail chips"

calls.call: The three bare ">" lines (How this changed, More, Built from) are now one "Details" row, drawn like the app's fold-out rows with the arrow at the right.
calls.why: Small labels on the row say what is inside. A row with nothing to add has no Details row.
calls.decided: "we don't use the bare > dropdowns anywhere"

calls.call: No underlined links are left anywhere on a deck. "Since last round" is a plain sentence; related decks and undo are small outlined buttons.
calls.why: Cost: the counts no longer jump to their rows. The headings inside each list replace that.
calls.decided: "nor the linked underline text at the top of the page"

calls.call: Taking a comment away is a bin, not an ×. In History, each earlier round is the same fold-out row.
calls.why: In the app × means close and a bin means remove.

calls.call: Phone width, before and after.
calls.why: Tiles are narrower there, as in the app.

calls.call: Not matched yet: the deck still opens in the Midnight colours, not your current theme, and the popup's Close is a word button where the app uses an ×.
calls.why: Your current theme has no colours in the deck tool yet. Say if either should change.

steps.intro: Judge here (not reviewed yet): are the fixes right, and is anything I left alone wrong to leave? You asked for reviewers with no background. Three ran: two code reviewers and a first-time tester. One helper then fixed what they found.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Fixes you will see

calls.call: Pressing a row's pencil a second time no longer deletes your comment. A small bin beside the comment removes it.
calls.why: The tester lost a comment this way with no warning.

calls.call: A status you change gets an outline and a "changed from" line. The pill is larger, with a small arrow.
calls.why: A changed row looked the same as an untouched one, and the pill read as a label.

calls.call: The option you pick gets a strong outline and a tick.
calls.why: It was a faint tint, the same look as "Recommended".

calls.call: The finish page says "Page 2, Question 3 of 3" and shows option names. A list you left alone reads "Left as listed".
calls.why: It showed internal labels and "Yes, build it" for lists you never touched.

calls.call: A background-only list is never counted as answered and never appears on the finish page.
calls.why: It was recorded as "Yes, build it".

calls.call: After Submit, every box is locked.
calls.why: One typing box still took text, which was then lost.

calls.call: A tiny accidental drag on a picture draws nothing.
calls.why: It left an empty, nearly invisible comment.

calls.call: At phone width the title has its own line and every button is tall enough to tap.
calls.why: The progress bar covered the title.

calls.call: A wording page opens zoomed to fit the window, with a count of your edits above the screen.
calls.why: On a short window the popup's foot is still cut off until you scroll.

calls.call: Two saves landing at once can no longer lose answers, and a late save can no longer undo your Submit.
calls.why: Found by the code reviewer; proven with a test of many saves at once.

calls.call: Page comments and status changes survive when the deck recovers from its backup copy.
calls.why: They were dropped; only answers came back.

calls.call: A saved screen is scrubbed of anything that can run or load from the internet before it enters a deck.
calls.why: A saved screen is a copy of a real page; it should be only words and layout.

calls.call: Recording stops if you close the tab mid-sentence or the voice helper fails.
calls.why: The microphone could stay open. Tested with a pretend microphone only.

calls.call: No web page outside this computer can read or change a deck's answers.
calls.why: The reviewer tried five ways in; all were refused.

calls.call: 16 automatic tests added, none removed: 445 in all, all passing.
calls.why: Each new test repeats one of the faults above and proves it stays fixed.

steps.intro: Judge here: five decisions that block or shape what comes next.

steps.headline: May I tell the safety scanner to ignore five made-up ids?
steps.today: 16 saved steps of this work exist only on this computer. The scanner that guards every backup refuses to send them.
steps.problem: One old step holds five practice-app ids that look like passwords to the scanner. They are not secrets, and I am not allowed to rewrite saved history.
steps.proposal: Yes adds those five exact lines to the scanner's ignore list and backs everything up. Nothing else is loosened. No leaves the work on this computer only.

steps.path: The checks menu before a build
steps.headline: Which reviewers should be on by default?
steps.today: The new rules give every build a checks menu where each reviewer is suggested on or off. Nothing says which are normally on.
steps.checked: Counted across 32 past builds: the code reviewer made 241 findings, about two thirds accepted. About half the first-time tester's findings were noise. The grader changed nothing.
steps.problem: You asked to discuss this. Without a default, each chat guesses.
steps.proposal: Pick the default. You can still flip any switch on any build.

options.label: Code reviewer always on; the rest suggested per build
pros: Keeps the one that reliably finds real faults.
The tester runs only when there are new screens.
cons: I judge when the tester is worth it, and can judge wrong.

options.label: Code reviewer and first-time tester always on
pros: This round the tester found real faults the code reviewers missed.
cons: Slower builds, and about half its findings are noise I must sort.

options.label: Nothing on by default
cons: A fault like "second press deletes your comment" reaches you instead of a reviewer.

steps.path: A deck link opened again after Submit
steps.headline: What should reopening an answered deck do?
steps.today: The link dies on Submit. If I serve the deck again, it opens empty and your earlier answers are filed beside it.
steps.problem: The tester read the empty deck as lost answers, and could have answered twice.
steps.proposal: Pick what a reopened deck shows.

options.label: Your answers, still editable, with a line saying when you sent them
pros: You can correct one answer and send again.
cons: A second Submit replaces the first; the first is kept in a dated file.

options.label: Your answers, locked
cons: In August a locked deck read to you as "I can't click through".

steps.headline: On a phone, how should commenting on part of a picture start?
steps.today: Since this round's fixes a finger dragged across a picture draws a comment area. Before, a finger could not draw at all.
steps.problem: A swipe that starts on a picture now draws instead of scrolling the page. Not tried on a real phone.
steps.proposal: Pick how drawing starts on a touch screen. A mouse is unaffected.

options.label: Tap a "Comment on an area" button, then drag
Leave it: any drag draws
cons: On a page of large pictures, scrolling means aiming for the gaps.

options.label: No drawing on phones
cons: On a phone you describe the spot in words again.
